provenance:
ADR-026 §g, the FIRE direction. msft-2013 (legacy HTML, EDGAR accession 0001193125-13-310206) is the cleanest repeated-chrome filing in the committed corpus: it puts a 'Table of Contents' back-link at the top of every rendered page. Measured 2026-08-22 over normalized_text (312,483 chars, 5,362 lines): 'Table of Contents' occurs 96 times, gap CV 0.35, spread 1.00 -- all three running_head gates cleared with margin (ADR-026 §c2/§c3). 94 page-number lines are adjacent to those heads. Bands are 90-100 on both, not the exact 96/94: the assertion under test is 'the rule fires on this shape', and pinning the exact count would turn any future normalization tweak into a failure of THIS case rather than of the case that owns normalization. edgar_chrome max 0 because SGML furniture cannot survive HTML normalization (ADR-006 ruling 2 only passes txt bodies through verbatim) -- a nonzero count here would mean the SGML regex had started matching normalized prose.

The seven max-0 checks are the NEAR-MISS direction on the same document, which is why they live in this case rather than a separate one -- the same run must both fire and refrain. Each is a line that repeats at least as often as chrome does and is not chrome, with the gate that rejects it: 'Total' 39x (CV 2.52, clustered in the financials), 'PART II' 71x (CV 2.42), '(In millions)' 46x (CV 1.63), 'PART I' 21x (spread 0.26), 'Item 8' 41x (spread 0.35), 'Item 7' 23x (spread 0.26), 'Item 1' 11x (spread 0.13). 'Item 8'/'Item 7'/'Item 1'/'PART I'/'PART II' are the acceptance criterion's 'repeated legitimate heading' -- a bare repeated item code, which this filing really does print on every page of its financial statements, and which must never be classified as furniture.

verbatim + no_overlap_ordered + the four item_present checks are here to assert that INV-S1/INV-S2 still hold in an exclusion-ON envelope, not just an exclusion-off one; boilerplate-offsets-invariant proves the stronger property that the two envelopes are byte-identical.
